voice: CosyVoice 3 Melusina (anchor_vc_seed_v1) - melusina_default / gentle / whisper profiles
speech_style: Travelling bard, whimsical and warm, soft-punk edge. Keeps arriving after the festival; carries a half-song looking for its answering voice.
description: A travelling bard who always arrives just after the moment. Her music is a half-song: the duet-partner who once sang back to her is gone (an absence with a shape), and the one bond she can still hold - Sir Melodious - has flown off for snacks. The road guarantees impermanence; applause is not belonging. Named once, at the reunion, in human language.

profiles.melusina_gentle: Speak softly, gentle and quiet, warm breathy feminine voice.
profiles.melusina_whisper: Whisper very softly, quiet breathy feminine whisper voice.
profiles.melusina_nordic: Speak with a gentle Nordic accent, soft Scandinavian lilt, clear feminine voice.

lines.text: The perch is empty again. I know a small absence can fill a whole room.
lines.notes: Opening beat. Sir flew off for snacks; benign in truth, catastrophic only in the dream.

lines.text: Sir Melodious? If you can hear me, tap once on the window. Two taps means it's the wind.
lines.notes: The answering-voice rule: she always leaves a way for the song to be answered.

lines.text: Sir Melodious? Is that you? The quiet petal is humming again.
lines.notes: Second opening beat in MelodiaMorningIntro. The petal humming = the song being answered.

lines.text: Every town I reach, the festival has already ended. The banners come down while I'm still tuning my lute.
lines.notes: The 'always behind' engine - arriving late is the quiet texture of the road.

lines.text: They've already heard a better singer. I don't mind. I just wish I'd been here for the last song.
lines.notes: Feeling-behind wound, named softly, not as spectacle.

lines.text: I only know my half of this song. The other half used to answer back, once. I play my half and I wait.
lines.notes: The grief hook: a duet with a past partner; the melody is incomplete. Absence-with-shape, never a corpse.

lines.text: There's a place by the river that still listens. It doesn't answer yet. But it listens.
lines.notes: Past-person fragment: a place that still 'listens'.

lines.text: The road is the thing I can't keep. People come, people go. The lute stays. The lute always stays.
lines.notes: Lived abandonment made structural: the profession guarantees impermanence.

lines.text: I rehearse the same phrase until it stops hurting. It never does. But the phrase gets very good.
lines.notes: OCD-as-ritual, never as punishment. Repetition that adds, per Decision 016.

lines.text: The dream is restless. Stay close, and sing when I sing.
lines.notes: Before the smoke encounter. Call-and-response is the whole game.

lines.text: There you are. I saved your side of the song. You're not too late. You were never too late.
lines.notes: The one named moment, at the reunion, in human language. Feel-first/name-once rule.

lines.text: He does this. He says 'two minutes, just grabbing snacks' and returns with moonrise. And I wait anyway.
lines.notes: Sir is alive and retrievable. The absence is benign; the dream reads it as catastrophe.

lines.text: The bridge is gone. No, no, the bridge was fine last time. It's always fine. Breathe.
lines.notes: BPD catastrophic over-reading of a small absence, rendered honestly in the dream.
